entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
William Melton was the 43rd Archbishop of York from 1317 until his death in 1340, and the first Lord Privy Seal. He played a pivotal role in the governance of the Kingdom of England during the reign of King Edward II.

As Archbishop, Melton was instrumental in the suppression of heresy and the promotion of Catholic orthodoxy. He also oversaw the implementation of the Statute of Pleading, a significant legal reform that aimed to clarify the procedures for trial by jury.

Melton's tenure as Lord Privy Seal saw the introduction of the first English-language version of the Statute of Pleading, which had a lasting impact on the development of English law. His legacy as a leading figure in the governance of England during the 14th century has endured for centuries.

Despite the passing of time, Melton's influence on the course of English history remains a testament to his enduring impact on the nation's legal and political systems.
